title: Farnunsa Creative Mother and Chief of Creation
classification: Historical Event / Mythology
body:
Farnunsa 

Creative Mother and Chief of Creation 

Domain: Creation, Life, Beauty, Stewardship, Divine Purpose

I have spent the better part of my life in the company of scholars who speak of the Elyndarûm with the careful detachment of those cataloguing the properties of stone or water. I cannot do this with Farnunsa. To write of her with detachment would be a kind of lie, and she is the last being in all of Anorvalas to whom I would offer a lie. She walks among us still. I have seen her, not as a rumour carried by trembling lips from some distant battlefield, but with these eyes, in the silver glade outside our city's eastern gate, moving between the Vardalum trees she herself caused to grow, touching the bark of each one the way a parent touches the face of a sleeping child. I set down my scrolls and knelt, and she looked at me the way the sun looks at everything: without favoritism, without distance, with a warmth so total it becomes indistinguishable from the air itself.

She made us from the essence of Anorvalas. This is the line that appears in every record, repeated so often it has begun to sound like furniture, present but unnoticed. I would ask anyone who has grown accustomed to that sentence to sit with it. She did not assemble us from materials. She did not speak a word and step back to observe what emerged. She reached into the living substance of the world she loved and she drew us out of it, which means that whatever Anorvalas is, its beauty, its balance, its ancient patience is also what we are made of. We are not inhabitants of this world. We are expressions of it. This is what she meant when she told our earliest ancestors that their purpose was stewardship. She was not assigning a role. She was describing our nature.

Her intervention in the matter of Ryuuaon's transgression in the creation of the beastmen, that obscene defiance of the harmony she had spent ages building with the other Gods was not wrath. I want to be precise about this because later generations may read the punishment she enacted and mistake its severity for anger. It was not anger. I have been in her presence enough times to know that anger is not among her instruments. What she enacted was correction, the precise, measured response of an architect who discovers that one of her collaborators has begun undermining the foundations. The souls she removed from Ryuuaon's domain and bound into the first undead were not a cruelty. They were an attempted repair. That Ryuuaon then cursed those same souls out of spite is the truest illustration of the difference between them.

She still teaches us. Not with lectures she is not a lecturer but by being present in the world in a way that reminds us what presence means. She is in the way the Vardalum trees respond to music sung beneath them. She is in the moment when a craftsman sets down a finished work and feels, for a breath, that it is exactly what it should be. The elves were made to notice these things, and she made us that way deliberately. Farnunsa does not need temples. She needs a people who have not forgotten how to pay attention.

title: Gyunshin Light Bringer and Shining Beacon
classification: Historical Event / Mythology
body:
Gyunshin 

Light Bringer and Shining Beacon 

Domain: Light, the Sun, Revelation, Clarity, Truth

The month of Valandarië belongs to Gyunshin in the way that a river belongs to its source, not through ownership but through origin. When the sun reaches the height of its arc and the land blazes with the fullness of its gift, every elf alive feels the particular quality of warmth that is his signature, not merely heat, but the specific illumination that makes things visible that were obscured the moment before. This is his domain, and it extends far beyond the literal sun. Gyunshin is the god of things becoming known. Of shadows retreating. Of the moment when you understand something you could not understand before, and the world rearranges itself around that understanding.

In this age, while the gods still walk openly among us and our cities rise white and brilliant under their guidance, Gyunshin's influence is perhaps the most woven into our daily life of all the Elyndarûm. The architects of what will one day be called the great houses, those among us who are already dreaming in marble and light, speak of designing their halls so that darkness has no purchase, no corner where it can pool and deepen. I have attended these planning councils and heard the arguments made in purely aesthetic terms, in terms of beauty and proportion, and I have sat quietly knowing that what they are actually doing is building prayers to Gyunshin without recognizing them as such. A hall that admits no shadow admits no secrets. They have absorbed his teaching without knowing they received it.

His relationship with Kelviirros is the most instructive opposition in the divine order. They are not enemies in the way that soldiers are enemies, Gyunshin does not pursue Kelviirros or seek to destroy him. He simply shines, and what cannot endure the light reveals itself by withdrawing from it. Kelviirros understands this better than anyone; his most effective work is always done in the spaces where elves have grown comfortable enough with a particular shadow that they stop noticing it is there. Gyunshin's answer to this is not a targeted assault but a constant, indiscriminate brilliance that asks nothing and illuminates everything. It is a form of divine patience that I find, the older I grow, increasingly difficult to distinguish from wisdom.

I will record one personal observation, offered not as theology but as testimony. I was present at the first lighting of the great beacon fire on the solstice eve three years past, when the flame was carried to the pyre by the eldest of the Alarion sages and the whole city gathered in the square beneath an open sky. When the fire caught and the light rose, there was a moment, I have asked others who were present and they confirm it when the stars seemed to lean closer. As if the act of making light on the ground had reminded something vast and attentive that we were here, and still trying. I believe that moment was Gyunshin answering.

title: Vallendirr Strong and Infinite in Will
classification: Historical Event / Mythology
body:
Vallendirr

Strong and Infinite in Will 

Domain: Endurance, Craft, Honor, Resilience, The Unyielding

There is a story told among the youngest of our craftspeople barely old enough to hold a hammer properly, about the first elf who tried to shape metal and failed. Who heated and struck and quenched and found the blade crooked, and tried again, and found it brittle, and tried again, and found it dull. The story goes that on the seventh failure, a presence settled beside the forge that had not been there before. Not a voice. Not an instruction. Simply a weight of attention, patient and absolute, that communicated without words: again. The young craftspeople nod when they hear this story because they have felt that presence themselves, standing over failed work in the small hours, and have found that they could not walk away from it. That is Vallendirr. Not the god of success. The god of again.

He shaped the dwarves alongside Kilbindar, and in doing so answered a question I have long held about the nature of divine creation: what is left when you remove the gift of immortality and the direct mentorship of the gods? What does a people become when they must find their way through hardship alone? The dwarves are Vallendirr's answer. Every impossible hall they have carved from stone without guidance, every beastman incursion they have beaten back through sheer refusal to yield, every generation that has looked at the walls their parents built and decided to build something greater — this is the curriculum of a god who believes that the most important lesson cannot be taught, only endured. The elves received their gifts directly. The dwarves received the capacity to earn them. I am not certain which of us was given the greater treasure.

He also co-created the orcs with Shilvaon, and his contribution to them is visible in the places their culture most differs from what our scholars expect. The orcish warrior who fights on past the point where pain has become irrelevant, the orcish chieftain who holds a decision long past the point where a human would have broken under the pressure of it, the orcish people who have survived centuries of neglect and isolation and emerged not broken but harder, this is Vallendirr's mark. He does not give comfort. He gives the capacity to continue without it.

I have met him once. I want to be careful about this claim because I am a scholar and scholars are meant to be precise about what they know versus what they believe. But there was an afternoon, four winters ago, when I had been working on a translation of a Vilyanor text for seven months and had come to a passage I could not crack, a passage that made everything preceding it nonsensical and everything following it unreadable. I sat with it until the candle burned down and then I sat in the dark with it. And then something in the room changed quality. Not warmth, the opposite of warmth. A cold steadiness, like standing in the shadow of a mountain. And in that stillness I found the translation. I cannot prove it was him. But I recorded it here because I think he would find the uncertainty appropriate.

title: Kilbindar Ethereal Bestowed and Magical Paladin
classification: Historical Event / Mythology
body:
Kilbindar

Ethereal Bestowed and Magical Paladin  

Domain: Magic, Protection, Divine Order, Precision 

Magic in this age, and I write this knowing that later scholars may struggle to fully grasp what I mean is not what it will become when the gods will have retreated and the flow of divine energy has thinned to what mortal practice alone can sustain. In this age, magic is abundant in the way that air is abundant, present in everything, flowing through the hands of any elf who has learned to receive it, capable of works that would be called miracles in any other context but here are simply called Tuesday afternoon. A young elf of modest talent can hold a conversation with a tree. A trained mage can reshape the course of a river. An elder of House Sylvaris can call a storm and then put it away when it is no longer needed. This abundance is Kilbindar's gift, and it is important to understand that it came with a warning, delivered directly, in his own words, to the first elves who received it: this will not always be this easy. Learn while it is.

He appeared to the Council of the Seven Great Houses in physical form during the campaign against the undead. Armoured, luminous, utterly still in the way that only beings of immense power manage to be still. I was not present for this; I record it from accounts given by those who were, whose testimony I have no reason to doubt. What strikes me most in their descriptions is not his appearance but his method of instruction. He did not demonstrate the Wards of Eternity and expect the elves to replicate them. He taught them. He walked them through the underlying principles. He asked questions and waited for answers and asked harder questions when the first answers proved shallow. He treated our most senior sages, beings of centuries of arcane study, as students, which they were, in his presence and he did so without condescension. This tells me something essential about his nature, he is a god who believes in the intelligence of those he teaches.

The magic he gifted us is not merely power. This distinction matters enormously and I wish our youngest students understood it more deeply than they currently do. Kilbindar's gift is structured, it has grammar, it has logic, it has rules that are not arbitrary constraints but descriptions of how power actually behaves when handled with precision. The elves who treat magic as a force to be grabbed and wielded will always be less capable than those who treat it as a language to be learned. This is because Kilbindar himself treats it as a language. His armor, described by every witness as gleaming with celestial light, is not decoration, it is function. He wears his power expressed outward as a teacher wears knowledge, not to display it, but because it is simply what he is.

I should note, for completeness, that he shares the creation of the dwarves with Vallendirr, and his contribution to them, the structural instinct, the sense that tells a great smith where the metal wants to go, the deep knowledge of how stone bears weight is the least acknowledged of all his gifts, since the dwarves rarely name him. But the precision in their finest work, the way their greatest halls have a geometric logic that feels almost magical despite being built without magic, bears his mark as clearly as any enchantment. Kilbindar is not the kind of god who requires acknowledgment. He requires excellence. And the dwarves, in their finest moments, provide it.

title: Shilvaon Singer of Nature and King of Life
classification: Historical Event / Mythology
body:
Shilvaon

Singer of Nature and King of Life  

Domain: Nature, Cycles of Life and Death, Harmony, the Wild 

When I was a child, very young, before formal study had taught me to hold experience at arm's length and examine it, I lay in the grass of a forest glade for an entire afternoon and listened. Not to anything in particular. To everything at once, the argument of two insects, the complaint of a branch settling under its own weight, the conversation of water over stone some distance away that I could feel more than hear, the particular silence of a predator moving through undergrowth in a direction that would not concern me. I fell asleep in that glade and woke knowing, without being told, that I was not the most important thing in it. This is, I have come to believe, the central lesson of Shilvaon. And he taught it to me when I was too young to resist learning it.

He led the first elves into the forests and taught them to hear what the world was saying. The accounts are consistent on the method, he did not explain. He walked with them in silence and waited for them to begin noticing. A god of lesser patience would have lectured. Shilvaon understood that the knowledge he was offering could not be transmitted through language, it had to be experienced, which meant it could only be received at the pace of the individual receiving it. Our greatest druids, those elves whose attunement to the natural world is so complete that they seem less like inhabitants of the forest than extensions of it, speak of their practice not as mastery but as listening. This vocabulary traces directly to his teaching. He did not give us dominion over nature. He gave us the humility to understand that nature was not waiting for our dominion.

His co-creation of the orcs with Vallendirr is a fact that some among our scholars discuss with discomfort, as though the orcs' capacity for violence somehow reflects poorly on him. I find this reading naive. Shilvaon is the King of Life, which means he is also, necessarily, the king of everything life requires to sustain itself, including struggle, predation, death as a passage rather than an endpoint, and the fierce territorial instincts that keep populations in balance. The orcs carry his gifts honestly. Their reverence for the cycle of life and death, their bone-deep connection to the lands they inhabit, their understanding that strength is not separate from the natural order but an expression of it. That some among them have been turned toward corruption by the whispers of darker gods is a grief Shilvaon carries. I have seen it in the way the forests near orcish lands sometimes go quiet in a way that feels like mourning.

He sings still, though fewer of us hear him as clearly as the first elves did. The druids of House Sylvaris hear him most faithfully, and they have built an entire tradition around the discipline of staying quiet enough to do so. In this age, while the gods are near and the flow of divine energy runs strong and uncorrupted, his song is in everything: in the way the Vardalum trees lean toward music, in the way wounded animals find their way to the clearings where our healers work, in the way the seasons turn with a precision that feels, if you are paying attention, less like mechanism and more like intention. He is not a distant king. He is the hum beneath all living things, present and patient, asking only that we do not mistake our own noise for silence.

title: Onnaih Yor Knower of All That Shall Not Be Known, Guide of the Shore
classification: Historical Event / Mythology
body:
Onnaih Yor

Knower of All That Shall Not Be Known, Guide of the Shore  

Domain: Forbidden Knowledge, Mystery, Thresholds, the Passage Between 

There is a certain kind of question that, when you ask it aloud, changes the room. Not because the room responds, rooms do not respond, but because the act of voicing it makes visible something that was present but unacknowledged, the way lighting a candle in a dark space does not create the furniture but merely reveals it. Onnaih Yor is the god of those questions. She is the Knower of All That Shall Not Be Known, which is a title that takes years to properly understand. It does not mean she withholds knowledge from us out of cruelty or hierarchy. It means she holds, in her custody, the knowledge that would unmake us if we received it before we were ready and she judges readiness with a patience that operates on timescales most elves cannot hold in mind without becoming dizzy.

She is also the Guide of the Shore, and the Shore in question is not a geographical feature but a threshold, the boundary between what is and what comes after, between the living world and whatever lies beyond Ryuuaon's domain, between understanding and the vast silence on the other side of it. She stands at this boundary not as a gatekeeper preventing passage but as a guide ensuring that passage, when it comes, is navigated with full awareness. The elves, being immortal, do not often require her guidance in the matter of death, but the scholars among us who have pushed their studies to the edge of what can be safely known, who have reached the boundary between illuminated knowledge and the dark beyond it, speak of encountering her presence at that edge with unmistakable consistency. She is there. She does not stop you. She watches, and her watching has the quality of someone who has seen this particular step taken before and knows both what it costs and what it earns.

In this age, while the gods are present and the free flow of divine magic means that even relatively inexperienced elves can reach further into the arcane than they perhaps should, Onnaih Yor serves a function I have come to regard as perhaps the most important in the entire divine order. She is the reason there are things we do not know. Not through failure or limitation, but through design. Farnunsa created us with the capacity for wisdom but also with the capacity for hubris, and Onnaih Yor is the balance, the presence that holds in reserve the knowledge that hubris would seize and use to unmake everything wisdom built. House Vilyanor, in their deepest archival work, have developed rituals of approach for certain categories of ancient knowledge that are, in their structure, prayers to Onnaih Yor, asking not for access to what lies beyond the boundary but for the discernment to know whether they are ready to cross it.

I have asked her a question directly, once. I will not record the question here, it is the kind of question that should not be written down and then left in a place where younger minds might find it… but I will record her answer, which was “not yet”. Two words. But the weight of them. The "not yet" of Onnaih Yor does not mean the same thing as the "not yet" of a teacher who is managing a lesson plan. It means, I see the full arc of what you are asking and what receiving it would do to you, and the version of you that needs this answer does not exist yet, but it will, and when it does I will already be here. I left that encounter feeling, for the first time in my long life, genuinely patient.

Provider of Warmth and Guide of Love  

Domain: Love, Warmth, Hearth, Community, Creative Devotion 

Our cities, in this age of their first rising, are not merely engineering. Anyone who has watched an elven city being built, really watched, not merely observed the logistics, knows this. There is a moment in the construction of every great hall, every communal plaza, every garden designed for gathering rather than solitude, when the work stops being about structure and starts being about something harder to name. When the craftspeople pause, not from fatigue, but from a kind of recognition as though the thing they are making has suddenly told them what it wants to be. In those moments, the air carries a quality I have learned to identify after years of attention, something warm and attending, like the feeling of being known by someone who loves you. That is Hynesta, and she is as present in this age as any of the Elyndarûm, though she announces herself the least loudly.

She is the god of both the hearth and the heart, which sounds like a simple pairing until you sit with it long enough to understand that they are not two things but one. The warmth that holds a family in place around a shared fire is the same force that drives a sculptor to spend a decade on a single work because they cannot bear to abandon it before it reaches the truth they see in it. Love, in Hynesta's conception, is not a feeling that happens to you. It is a practice of devotion, a willingness to return, again and again, to the thing or the person or the work that you have claimed as yours to care for. She is the god who makes commitment feel not like a cage but like a home.

The music we make in this age, and I write this with awareness that later scholars may have only fragments of it, because the music of the Aevum Primordialis was made under the direct hearing of the gods and reached into registers of beauty and power that I am not certain can be recovered if the divine proximity fades, our music is Hynesta's most visible gift. Not because she invented music; Shilvaon gave us the capacity to hear the world's song. But the quality that makes elven music different from mere skilled performance is her gift, the quality of love poured into the making of it, the devotion of a singer who is not performing for an audience but offering something to the world. The artifacts we have made under the gaze of the gods carry a similar quality. They are not merely objects of power. They are objects of care. And care, in sufficient concentration, becomes its own kind of magic.

She visited me on the night my mentor died. I was not prepared for grief, none of us are, even knowing it is coming, and I sat in the dark of my study with the particular cold of a loss that has not yet fully declared itself, the cold that comes before the full understanding arrives. She did not appear in any dramatic form. The candles, which had gone out, relit themselves one by one without wind or hand, and the room became warm. Not supernaturally warm, just the warmth that a room has when it is occupied by someone who is glad to be in it. I sat in that warmth for a long time and I understood, in the way you understand things in the presence of gods, that grief and love are not opposites. They are the same thing, measured from different ends. She stayed until I was ready for morning.

title: Ayondun Dol Keeper of Justice and Order, Seer of Mercy
classification: Historical Event / Mythology
body:
Ayondun Dol

Keeper of Justice and Order, Seer of Mercy  

Domain: Justice, Order, Balance, Mercy, Divine Law 

The least celebrated of the Elyndarûm among the common people, and by common I mean those who have not made the study of the divine their life's work, is almost certainly Ayondun Dol, and this neglect is itself a kind of tribute to his effectiveness. Justice, when it functions as it should, is invisible. You do not notice the presence of right consequence any more than you notice the weight of the sky; it is only when it fails, when wrong acts proceed without answer and the balance tilts and tilts until it becomes impossible to pretend the tilt is not there, that you understand what was being provided all along. While the gods walk among us and the divine order is young enough to still carry the full clarity of its original design, Ayondun Dol is the quiet architecture beneath everything else.

His role in the punishment of Ryuuaon following the creation of the beastmen is the most documented of his direct interventions, and I have studied those accounts with care. What strikes me is not the severity of the response, which was considerable, but its precision. Farnunsa provided the creative power required to wrench souls from Ryuuaon's domain. Ayondun Dol provided the judicial authority, and the determination of appropriate consequence, the calibration of punishment to transgression, the structure that ensured the act was correction rather than retaliation. Without him, Farnunsa's grief and anger at the transgression might have produced a response disproportionate to its purpose. With him, the punishment was exactly what it needed to be, severe enough to constitute a genuine diminishment of Ryuuaon's power, measured enough to preserve the overall balance rather than shatter it. This precision is his gift and his nature.

His epithet includes Seer of Mercy, which surprises those who encounter it for the first time, because mercy and justice are so often spoken of in opposition. But this opposition is a misunderstanding that Ayondun Dol's existence corrects. Mercy, in his conception, is not the suspension of consequence but the fullest possible understanding of it, the insistence on knowing not just what happened but why, not just the act but the full weight of the circumstances that produced it, before determining what the right response looks like. A judge who cannot be moved by context is not just; they are mechanical. Ayondun Dol is the god who holds both the law and the living being before the law in his attention simultaneously, and whose judgments account for both.

I will note something that troubles me and that I record here because I believe honest scholarship requires the recording of uncertainty alongside certainty. Ayondun Dol's quiet work keeps the balance in ways we perhaps take too readily for granted. I find myself wondering, in my more anxious hours, what happens to justice if the gods retreat, if his sustaining attention is no longer present in the world's daily operation and the balance must be maintained, if it is to be maintained at all, by mortal hands alone. I have no answer to this. I record the question because I think it is the right question to be holding, and because Ayondun Dol, of all the Elyndarûm, strikes me as the one most likely to appreciate a mortal who has identified the correct thing to worry about.

title: Janvirrtal Hero of Old and Free of the Deep
classification: Historical Event / Mythology
body:
Janvirrtal 

Hero of Old and Free of the Deep  

Domain: Sacrifice, Freedom, Courage, Divine Ascension 

I knew him. I want to begin with that, because every other account I have read of what happened at the Wraetian Range treats it as history, as event, as the kind of thing that is written down and then referenced from a distance. I cannot write it from a distance. I was there. I was younger then, not young, but younger, and I was part of the scholarly contingent that accompanied the war host in a recording capacity, because House Vilyanor believed, correctly, that whatever happened in those mountains would need to be remembered precisely. What I did not anticipate, and what none of us had the foresight to prepare for, was that what happened would be the kind of thing that resists precise recording, because it took place at the intersection of the mortal world and something so far beyond it that language becomes approximate.

The Zahkaran were unlike anything the elves had faced. I have searched for comparisons and found none that are adequate, so I will describe rather than compare. They were vast, each one standing twice the height of the tallest elf, and they were wreathed in a darkness that was not merely absence of light but active consumption of it, a void that swallowed illumination rather than leaving it aside. Around them the air turned cold in a way that reached past the skin into the spirit, a cold that was not temperature but dread given physical form. They burned with blue flame that produced no light. I watched a torch carried within fifteen feet of one simply cease to be lit, not blown out, not dimmed, simply no longer burning, as though fire itself had decided to be somewhere else. They moved through our ranks like a tide moves through sand — not through effort, but through a kind of irresistible belonging, as though destruction was simply their natural state and our army was a temporary inconvenience in an ongoing condition.

Janvirrtal was the lord of the host. I had known him as a military commander of exceptional skill, the kind of leader whose soldiers do not merely follow orders but become, in the field, extensions of his intention. What I watched him become in those final hours was something I do not have a category for, and I have spent the decades since attempting to construct one. As the elven lines began to fail, as the Zahkaran advanced and the host lost soldiers by the thousands and the mathematics of attrition became undeniable, he took the artifact his house had made, I had seen it before, a thing of terrible contained power, the kind of object that feels as though it is thinking about you when you hold it, and he climbed to the high point of the mountain range while the battle raged below him. Alone. I watched him go. I did not understand yet what I was watching.

What he did on that peak I can describe only in terms of what was visible from the position of a scholar standing in the middle of a battle and trying to keep his eyes open. He poured himself into the artifact, not metaphorically, not symbolically, but in some literal sense that I watched happen in real time, watching his light go into the object the way water goes into stone, and then the artifact opened. There is no better word. It opened, and what came out was not magic in any sense I had studied or witnessed before. It was the response of the universe to a sufficient act of selfless sacrifice. Farnunsa heard him, I believe this completely, based on what I witnessed, and she reached down and joined what was left of him in the power, and what struck the mountain struck it not as a weapon but as a testament. The light that hit the range that day carved the mithril veins the dwarves would one day find, locked the seven remaining Zahkaran in prisons of divine making deep in the stone, and left on the peak nothing but his house's banner, his sword, and an absence of the man who had held them. The elves we lost in that battle numbered in the thousands. The elves we did not lose because of what he did number in the tens of thousands. I sat on the mountainside afterward in the silence and I tried to understand what I had seen, and what I arrived at was this, that a mortal, through an act of perfect selflessness at sufficient magnitude, had briefly become indistinguishable from a god. The difference between that and what Janvirrtal now is turned out to be no difference at all.

title: Ryuuaon Keeper of the Deep and Plague of the Corrupt
classification: Historical Event / Mythology
body:
Ryuuaon

Keeper of the Deep and Plague of the Corrupt  

Domain: Death, Endings, Mortality, Corruption, the Depths 

I approach this entry with care, because Ryuuaon is the god whose nature has changed most drastically between his original design and his current expression, and because conflating what he was meant to be with what he has become is a scholarly error with real consequences. He was made as the Keeper of the Deep, the custodian of endings, the god who ensured that death was a passage and not an accumulation, that the souls of the departed moved onward rather than filling the living world until it could no longer sustain life. This is a necessary function. The divine order required it. Without a god of endings, creation becomes a slow suffocation under the weight of what refuses to conclude. Ryuuaon, in his original conception, was as essential to Anorvalas as Farnunsa. They were, in a sense, the same process viewed from opposite ends of a life.

What changed him, and I believe it was a process rather than an event, a gradual corruption rather than a single turning, was the discovery that mortality was a lever. That the knowledge of death could be used to produce behavior, desperation, hunger for legacy, the particular recklessness of beings who understand they have finite time and choose to fill it with conquest rather than wisdom. He whispered this knowledge into the hearts of the younger races, not as comfort but as a goad. Humans, dwarves, orcs, they all received from him the sharpened awareness of their own ending, framed not as a natural truth to be accepted but as an injustice to be raged against. This is the most insidious thing Ryuuaon does, he takes what is real and true… you will die, time is short, legacy is finite, and he presents it in a frame that produces ruin rather than meaning.

His collaboration with Kelviirros in creating the beastmen was the act that forced the divine order to respond directly, and the punishment delivered by Farnunsa and Ayondun Dol, the removal of thousands of souls from his domain, bound into the first undead, wounded him in a way that appears to have completed his corruption. The curse he placed on those same souls in retaliation is the act I return to when I need to understand what he has become. He took beings whose suffering was already immense, souls wrenched from rest and bound into decayed vessels, trapped between life and death and he made their suffering worse, specifically to spite Farnunsa. He used his own diminished charges as instruments of revenge. There is no reading of this act that reflects a god still operating within any conception of his original purpose.

I write this at a time when his influence is present but not dominant when the whispers he places in mortal hearts are one voice among several rather than the only voice being heard. I am aware, with a dread I will not pretend is merely academic, that this balance is not guaranteed to hold. The Zahkaran, those horrors of blue flameless fire and consuming shadow that Janvirrtal's sacrifice locked away in the deep stone, were made in the shadow of Ryuuaon's growing darkness. Creatures whose very presence swallows light, whose cold reaches past flesh into spirit, whose existence seems to constitute an argument that warmth and meaning were always temporary arrangements in a universe that is, at its core, empty. Ryuuaon did not make them alone. But they are, I think, what his vision of Anorvalas looks like from the inside.

title: Kelviirros Weaver of Shadows and Tempest of Lies
classification: Historical Event / Mythology
body:
Kelviirros

Weaver of Shadows and Tempest of Lies

Domain: Shadow, Ambition, Deception, Corruption, Whispered Ruin 

The first thing to understand about Kelviirros is that he is not stupid, and treating him as though he were is the most reliable path to being destroyed by him. He is the Weaver of Shadows and the Tempest of Lies, and his particular genius, I use that word deliberately and with full awareness of its implications, is that his most effective corruptions are built on foundations of truth. He does not tell the dwarves to abandon their honor. He tells them, accurately, that they built their civilization without divine guidance, and then asks them, with the gentlest possible inflection, why they should accept instruction from beings who have never had to work for anything they possess. He does not tell the humans that their elven mentors wish them harm. He simply points, accurately, to the things the elves have withheld, and allows human ambition to supply the motive he does not need to invent.

His origins within the Elyndarûm are the least documented of any of the divine order, and I believe this is deliberate, that Kelviirros has, over time, ensured the obscuring of the earliest accounts of his nature, because an accurate record of what he was before the corruption set in would make his methods transparent in ways that would reduce their effectiveness. What fragments remain suggest that he was, originally, the god of shadow in a neutral sense: of the spaces between things, of concealment as a necessary component of a functioning world, of the gap between what is visible and what is real. These are not inherently sinister domains. Shadows are restful. Mystery is generative. The space between words is where meaning lives. He was, perhaps, the god who kept Anorvalas from being too legible, too flat, too fully illuminated to sustain complexity.

What he has made of those domains is the question that should occupy every scholar of the divine order. Because the difference between the god of necessary shadow and the god who whispers corruption into every heart that harbors a wound is not a difference of domain but of intention, and somewhere, across ages of accumulated resentment at a divine order he apparently believes undervalued him, Kelviirros's intention turned. He works now not to preserve the complexity of shadow but to use it. His whispers are not invitations to mystery; they are targeted manipulations, precisely calibrated to the specific pride and specific wound of each recipient. He found what the dwarves feared. He found what the humans craved. He found the silence that the orcs had interpreted as divine abandonment and he explained it to them in the worst possible terms. He rarely lies outright. He does not need to. The truth, in his hands, becomes a weapon by virtue of how it is held.

His influence is still one force among many rather than the dominant voice in the world's ear, Kelviirros is most visible in the places where gifted elves begin to believe that their gifts entitle them to more than they have been given. I have seen it in our own scholars, the moment when genuine curiosity tips into something harder and more grasping, when the desire to know becomes the conviction that anything withheld is being withheld unjustly, when humility gives way to a sense of deprivation. This is his entry point, and it is always the same entry point, and it is always the one we are least prepared to defend because it disguises itself as a reasonable grievance. The defense against Kelviirros is not righteousness. It is honesty, the specific honesty of knowing your own pride well enough to recognize when something else has taken hold of it and begun to steer.

body:
Overview

Thalanir Væloryneth are trans-elvish AEN super-soldiers engineered to operate beyond the biological, environmental, and cognitive limits of even elite biogenic forces. They are designed for missions where conventional infantry, clone marines, or mechanized forces cannot sustain effectiveness, including prolonged vacuum exposure, extreme radiation fields, high-G combat insertions, and direct engagement with enemy super-assets. Thalanir Væloryneth function as autonomous combat entities capable of independent battlespace control, strategic decapitation, and sustained operations in isolation from fleet or command infrastructure.

Foundational genome selection: Thalanir Væloryneth are drawn solely from Elvish refined genetic stock, selected for the purity of lineage. Designed to complement conventional task groups rather than replace them, the Phantom excels at preparing the battlespace, it scouts enemy positions, seeds false signatures, disables critical sensors and datalinks, and provides target designation and preconditioning for strike assets while remaining off conventional engagement radars. When necessary it can strike selected targets with precision, exfiltrate assets, or act as an autonomous relay for clandestine comms. 


Survivability is achieved by concealment and avoidance rather than brute force sensor-masking suites, APBL micro-resonant dampers, adaptive thermal baffles, and signature-scrubbing conduits allow long-dwell penetration missions. A focused EW/cryptography stack lets the Phantom sever local networks, spoof hostile targeting, and create tactical uncertainty for adversaries. 


Thalanis vessels are assigned to Shadow Squadrons and deep reconnaissance wings, they operate in pairs or small cells for redundancy, feed tactical black data to fleet command, and perform mission types that require plausible deniability or strategic subtlety.

 THE HIGH REALM OF THE ELVES 

Office of the Sovereign Treasury • The Valarindë, the Council of the Seven Great Houses 

Anorvalas Ecumenopolis • Capital District, Seat of the First House

SUBJECT: Elenar Credit - Denomination Framework, Reserve Basis, and Strategic Valuation 

EFFECTIVE DATE: 4180.2, Anorvalas Standard 

DISTRIBUTION: All Member Worlds of Arandorë Eldainë • Registered Foreign Exchange Partners • Public Archive

I. PREAMBLE AND PURPOSE OF ISSUANCE 

This communiqué is issued by the Sovereign Treasury of Arandorë Eldainë under the authority of the Valarindë, the Council of the Seven Great Houses. It constitutes an official statement of monetary policy, reserve basis, and the strategic industrial rationale underpinning the three-tier denomination structure of the Elenar Credit.

Since the formal unification of the Seven Houses, the Elenar Credit has served as the sovereign currency of the High Realm. Its tiered structure of physical denominations, struck in gold, silver, and copper, predates the current age of deep-space expansion by millennia. Origins can be traced to the earliest material economies of Anorvalas during what historians of the Realm designate the Foundational Period, a time when the first standardized instruments of exchange were agreed upon between communities whose material needs and technological capacities differed vastly from those of the present age.

That this physical denomination structure has persisted into an era of interstellar travel and artificial cognition reflects not sentiment but deliberate and continuously renewed policy. At its core is the active management of industrial demand for each of the three metals, conducted in such a manner that their intrinsic scarcity remains a live economic reality rather than a historical artifact. To be precise on this point: the Elenar Credit is not backed by gold, silver, and copper in the manner of primitive monetary systems that pledged metals they had no particular need for. Rather, it is sustained by them, meaning that genuine, ongoing, and strategically cultivated demand for each metal across distinct domains of the Realm's industrial and technological base provides the foundation of each denomination's worth. These are not metals kept in vaults as symbols. They are metals the Realm actively requires and actively consumes.

Three purposes motivate the issuance of this communiqué. First, it reaffirms the reserve basis of each denomination for the benefit of member worlds, registered trading partners, and citizens of all designations within the Realm. Second, it addresses questions raised in recent cycles regarding the long-term viability of metal-based denomination in an age of advanced fabrication technology. Third, it articulates the formal position of the Valarindë on the relationship between the Elenar Credit's material basis and the Realm's broader strategic posture.

II. HISTORICAL BASIS

Before the unification of the Seven Houses, when the elven peoples of Anorvalas first established standardized exchange across the boundaries of their distinct communities, the earliest Elenar Credits were not struck in a mint but shaped by hand. Elves of the great houses, each brought their own traditions to those early negotiations. What emerged was less a designed system than an agreed one: denominations distinguished by metal content and the symbolic glyphs of the founding houses, valued because all parties had genuine and independent reasons to value the materials in question.

What is significant about this origin is not the crudeness of the early form but the sophistication of the underlying logic. Gold, silver, and copper were not chosen arbitrarily by the founding treasurers who served the unified Seven Houses. Each metal occupied a distinct and irreplaceable functional role in the technologies of that age, and a currency whose denominations corresponded to materials with genuine industrial necessity was understood to carry a natural resistance to debasement. No decree can make a metal more abundant than it is. An overissuing authority would find itself outpaced by its own industrial consumption. The founding generation grasped something that monetary theorists of less durable civilizations have repeatedly failed to learn: a currency is only as stable as the real demand for the thing that backs it, and the most reliable way to maintain that demand is to make the backing material genuinely indispensable.

 Spanning the unification of Anorvalas, the establishment of orbital infrastructure, the age of planetary colonisation, and the expansion into deep-space operations that defines the present era, the specific applications of each metal evolved substantially across the millennia that followed. Nothing that justified copper's value in the Foundational Period justifies it today; the same is true of gold and silver. What has not changed is the principle. At every stage of technological development, the Sovereign Treasury has worked in concert with the industrial ministries of the Seven Houses to ensure that each denomination metal remains embedded in a domain of genuine strategic necessity. Each generation of the Valarindë has renewed and reviewed this commitment, and where necessary reengineered it.

III. THE GOLD ELENAR

As the primary denomination of the Elenar Credit, the Gold Elenar is the unit in which the Realm's largest strategic transactions are conducted. Its reserve basis rests on the physical properties of gold that have made it indispensable to precision systems since the earliest age of the Realm's technological development: it does not corrode, it does not oxidize, and its conductivity does not degrade over time regardless of environmental conditions. At the scales relevant to advanced navigational and computational hardware, the failure of a single corroded contact is sufficient to compromise an entire circuit. Substitutes have been tested in each generation of the Realm's engineering practice, and none have performed adequately when exposed to the radiation, trace compounds, and thermal cycling that characterize operational conditions over the multi-century deployment timescales that elven infrastructure demands. 


All gold mining operations within Arandorë Eldainë's territorial space are licensed through the Sovereign Treasury under the Strategic Metals Act (Provision 14 of the Unification Charter), and export to non-member entities requires authorization at the Council level. The Gold Elenar is struck at the Sovereign Mint on Anorvalas as a rectangular tablet bearing the glyph of the High Houses on the obverse and the foundational runes of the Unification on the reverse. Each tablet constitutes a unit of currency and a standardized ingot of certified-purity gold, redeemable at any Sovereign Treasury facility for its full material value. No issuing authority can produce more Gold Elenars without proportionally depleting the Realm's stockpile of the material on which its most critical precision systems depend. 

IV. THE SILVER ELENAR

As the secondary denomination of the Elenar Credit, the Silver Elenar is the unit in which the majority of inter-house commercial transactions, licensed interstellar trade, and governmental procurement contracts are conducted. Its reserve basis is grounded in silver's unique suitability for prolonged contact with living tissue. Silver ions interact with biological membranes in a manner that suppresses bacterial colonization without triggering the immune responses that other metals provoke — a property understood in elven medicine since the Foundational Period and now foundational to the entire field of long-duration implant technology. Every device designed to remain within living tissue for decades requires components the body will not reject, corrode from within, or wall off in scar tissue. Silver is the only material that meets this standard reliably over the timescales that elven longevity demands.

Reserve management for silver is conducted in coordination with the Office of Biomedical Infrastructure against rolling demand projections, with a mandatory buffer reserve of not less than forty percent of projected demand held in certified Treasury storage. This buffer was formally elevated following the Korban invasion of the Outer Rim, during which Korban forces occupied several systems within Arandorë Eldainë's territorial space, disrupting raw material extraction across part of the Realm's silver supply chain until the Arandorë Eldainë Navy expelled the invaders and restored territorial integrity. The experience confirmed what the Treasury had long argued: forty percent is not a conservative threshold but a minimum one. The Valarindë has not reduced it since, and does not intend to. On its obverse, the Silver Elenar bears the Kilbindar glyph of the Magical Paladin, whose symbolic association with silver reaches back to the earliest ages of elven civilization.

V. THE COPPER ELENAR

Of all three denominations, the Copper Elenar is the most widely held and most immediately familiar to the broadest range of the Realm's population, serving as the unit of everyday commercial exchange across all member worlds. Its reserve basis is grounded in copper's role as the fundamental medium through which electrical power moves, a role it has held without serious challenge from the earliest age of elven engineering to the present. Copper carries current with lower resistive loss than any material available at practical scale, draws heat from surfaces faster than almost any solid conductor, and forms reliable joints with itself and most other engineering metals without specialist processing. Superconducting materials exist and are used where their properties justify the infrastructure required to sustain them within active fleet and planetary operations. Copper remains what it has always been, the material that works consistently, at any scale, under conditions the Realm is likely to actually encounter.


The breadth of copper's application means its consumption dwarfs that of gold and silver combined. Planetary power grids, atmospheric processors, fabrication cooling systems, and more runs on copper. Treasury demand projections are consistent across every scenario modelled: consumption grows with the Realm's expansion and does not plateau. Unlike gold and silver, copper extraction operates without standard export restriction, reflecting its greater abundance within Realm territorial space. A strategic reserve buffer is nevertheless maintained and reviewed annually. On its obverse, the Copper Elenar bears the Shilvaon glyph of the Singer of Nature, acknowledging copper's role as the invisible medium of connection and flow that sustains the Realm's infrastructure much like rivers sustain the land. 

VI. CLOSING STATEMENT OF THE VALARINDË

The Elenar Credit has endured because the peoples of Arandorë Eldainë have, in each generation, chosen institutions worthy of endurance. The metals in which it is struck were chosen by ancestors who understood that a currency must rest on something real: not merely valuable in the abstract, but necessary in the concrete, indispensable to the continued functioning of the civilization that relies on it.

 That founding choice has proven more durable than the technologies it originally supported, more durable than the specific applications that justified it in any given era, and more durable than the political configurations of the Realm across its long history of expansion, conflict, reformation, and renewal. Its durability has nothing to do with reverence for the past. In each generation, the Seven Houses have renewed the discipline of refusing to allow convenience or short-term pressure to erode the foundations on which lasting institutions are built. That renewal is the work, and it continues.

The Valarindë, the Council of the Seven Great Houses, commends this communiqué to the Realm's citizens, trading partners, and member worlds, and affirms its continued commitment to the monetary policies described herein.

POWERPLANT

The Talarion-II is powered by a vehicle-rated Calindor-class D-He3 fusion micro-reactor coupled to a hybrid electric drive train. The reactor provides continuous electrical power to the traction motors, weapon systems, sensors, Aurelion APBL defensive systems, and electronic warfare suite simultaneously without competing power demands. Regenerative braking through the traction motors recovers kinetic energy during deceleration and feeds it back into the vehicle's Tharëndal energy reserve.


The fusion reactor eliminates the fuel convoy dependency of combustion-powered vehicles. The vehicle operates for weeks on carried fuel canisters. Operational range is determined by track wear, suspension maintenance intervals, and crew endurance rather than fuel supply.

ARMAMENT

Main gun: 130 mm coilgun

The primary weapon is a 130 mm electromagnetic coilgun firing tungsten carbide kinetic penetrator rounds from an automated loading system. Sequential REBCO superconducting coils in the barrel accelerate the penetrator rod to hypervelocity, achieving muzzle velocities of 2,500 to 3,500 m/s depending on the selected charge profile. At these velocities, the kinetic energy per round far exceeds conventional chemical-propellant guns. ICAS-V computes the ballistic solution for local gravity, atmospheric density, wind, and target movement.


Coilgun rounds carry no propellant charge. Each round is a penetrator rod in a discarding sabot with no cartridge case and no chemical propellant. This makes each round substantially smaller and lighter than a conventional tank round, allowing the automated magazine to carry a significantly larger ammunition inventory than combustion-propellant vehicles of equivalent size.

A vehicle-rated pulsed laser mounted coaxially with the main gun, sharing the turret's stabilization and fire control. The coaxial laser provides rapid-response engagement of personnel, light vehicles, and small unmanned systems without expending kinetic ammunition. ICAS-V synchronizes the coaxial laser with the main gun for target preconditioning (degrading armor at the designated aim point before a kinetic round arrives, reducing the armor's effective resistance at the moment of kinetic impact).

LIMITATIONS

Kinetic ammunition is finite. The directed energy weapons draw from the reactor and require no ammunition resupply, but the 130 mm main gun's 60 to 80 round magazine is consumed during sustained armored engagement. Ammunition resupply is the vehicle's primary logistics requirement.


Mass limits terrain access. At 72 metric tons, the Talarion-II cannot cross all bridges, soft terrain, or steep grades that lighter vehicles can negotiate. Route planning accounts for the vehicle's ground pressure and mass.


Track and suspension wear limits range. The 2,000+ km operational range is determined by running gear endurance rather than fuel. Extended high-speed movement over rough terrain accelerates track and suspension wear, reducing the interval before maintenance is required.


Height limits concealment. At 3 m height, the Talarion-II presents a larger profile than lower-silhouette vehicles. Hull-down positioning (using the adaptive suspension to lower the hull behind terrain cover with only the turret exposed) mitigates this in defensive positions.

Fire missions from dismounted operators are received and processed by ICAS-V for engagement by the main gun or directed energy weapons.


Target Preconditioning: The coaxial laser degrades enemy armor at the designated aim point before the main gun fires. The laser induces thermal shock fracture in the target's ceramic armor layers at the point where the kinetic penetrator will arrive. The penetrator strikes armor that has already been cracked and weakened, reducing the effective resistance. ICAS-V manages the timing automatically: the laser fires, conditions the target, and the main gun fires when ICAS-V determines the armor at the aim point has been sufficiently degraded.


Urban Operations: The modular track units convert for urban terrain. The adaptive hydropneumatic suspension adjusts ride height for clearance under obstacles or hull-down positioning behind low cover. The remote weapon station provides 360° close-in defense against threats from upper floors, rooftops, and side streets while the main turret engages primary targets.


Logistics Footprint: Directed energy weapons drawing from the reactor require no ammunition resupply. The 130 mm coilgun rounds are the primary consumable. Resupply is delivered through logistics vehicles or orbital cargo pod drops using the Thaelindor-V cargo variant.

No dedicated air defense. The Nimrael carries no SAM capability. The main weapon's sweep mode provides close-in defense against drones and incoming munitions but cannot engage high-altitude or long-range aerial threats. Formation-level air defense depends on the Velendril's heavy SAMs.


Single emitter thermal limits. The single main weapon accumulates heat faster under sustained fire than the Velendril's alternating twin mount. Extended continuous engagement at high output requires managed firing pauses for thermal recovery. ICAS-V monitors emitter temperature and manages the duty cycle automatically.


Reconnaissance role increases exposure. Operating ahead of the main formation in reconnaissance-in-force missions places the Nimrael in contact before heavier platforms arrive in support. The lighter armor makes this inherently higher risk than leading with the Talarion-II.

OPERATIONAL NOTES

Combined Arms Role: The Nimrael fills the gap between the Talarion-II's heavy anti-armor capability and the Velendril's troop delivery and air defense role. The Nimrael provides rapid fire support, reconnaissance, and CIWS defense for the formation. In a combined-arms advance, the Nimrael scouts ahead or on the flanks, identifies threats, and engages targets of opportunity with its adaptive beam weapon while the Talarion-II delivers kinetic anti-armor effects and the Velendril delivers infantry and provides air defense umbrella.


Reconnaissance-in-Force: The Nimrael's lower profile, higher speed, and comprehensive sensor suite make it the preferred platform for probing enemy positions. The vehicle advances into contested terrain, collects sensor data, engages targets that can be defeated with directed energy, and reports contact data to the formation through the Laerithil relay and squad mesh network. The ICAS-V intelligence gathered during reconnaissance feeds directly into the Talarion-II and Velendril fire control systems for follow-on engagement.


CIWS Role: The adaptive beam weapon in sweep mode provides the Nimrael with organic close-in defense against drones, loitering munitions, and incoming guided missiles. In formation, the Nimrael extends this CIWS coverage to adjacent vehicles, protecting the Talarion-II from close-in aerial threats that the MBT's remote weapon station may not engage quickly enough.


Urban Operations: The narrower hull (3.5 m versus 4.0 m for the Talarion-II and Velendril) allows the Nimrael to navigate tighter urban corridors. The adaptive beam weapon transitions rapidly between anti-personnel, anti-vehicle, and CIWS modes as the threat environment changes from block to block. The lower profile reduces exposure above rooflines and wall cover.

body:
AEN Fleets — Formation Designations

(Standardized under Admiralty Codex Directive 04-VANYA)

Talon

  • Size: 3–5 vessels
  • Role: Smallest maneuver element — scout wing, picket, or hunter-killer patrol.
  • Typical Commander: Thalion (Lieutenant Commander)
  • Notes: Operates independently or as a reconnaissance spearhead for larger groups.

Lance

  • Size: 6–10 vessels
  • Role: Strike or escort detachment focused on precision operations or convoy defense.
  • Typical Commander: Aran (Commander)
  • Notes: Flexible enough for rapid response or forward screening. Often used for system patrol or expeditionary vanguard operations.

Battlegroup

  • Size: 12–25 vessels
  • Role: Core tactical formation for exploration, deep-space engagements; combines screening, strike, and carrier elements.
  • Typical Commander: Tanar (Captain)
  • Notes: Primary fleet maneuver element. Self-sufficient for limited-duration campaigns.

Task Force

  • Size: 30–60 vessels
  • Role: Multi-vector combat and operations element; combines multiple battlegroups under unified command.
  • Typical Commander: Rimbaer (Rear Admiral, Lower Half)
  • Notes: Can conduct independent fleet actions; forms the backbone of AEN rapid-deployment forces.

Fleet

  • Size: 100–200 vessels
  • Role: Full operational fleet; represents the main projection of power within a sector or theater.
  • Typical Commander: Rimbalen (Rear Admiral, Upper Half)
  • Notes: Self-sustaining for long campaigns; maintains dedicated carriers, repair platforms, and planetary assault elements.

Host

  • Size: 300–450 vessels
  • Role: Grand strategic formation capable of full planetary invasion, orbital control, or multi-system domination.
  • Typical Commander: Mithrand (Vice Admiral)
  • Notes: Includes dedicated command carriers and logistical trains; capable of simultaneous multi-system operations.

Grand Armada

  • Size: 700–1,200 vessels
  • Role: Major theater fleet; full multi-system force with dedicated planetary, carrier, and capital wings.
  • Typical Commander: Eldamar (Admiral)
  • Notes: Used for prolonged galactic-front engagements or major crusade-level offensives.

Celestial Host

  • Size: 1,500–2,500 vessels
  • Role: Apex formation of the Arandorë Eldainë Navy; total war echelon capable of sub-sector conquest or defense of home systems.
  • Typical Commander: Ambaron (Fleet Admiral) or Arandur Eäcalion (High Lord Admiral)
  • Notes: Represents the full might of the AEN. Deployed only under Conclave directive or existential threat. Capable of autonomous warfighting for years.

stats.val: Titanium-carbide alloy skeleton / modular composite armor shell

body:
Overview

Vaelindor Cognyr units are purpose-built combat droids engineered to augment and reinforce Caelyndor Marinyr marine squads in frontline assault operations. Unlike the clone trooper program, the Vaelindor Cognyr originates from an entirely separate engineering division with no shared development lineage, though its armor aesthetic has been deliberately aligned with marine visual identity to maintain cohesion on the battlefield and reduce friendly-fire risk in close-quarters environments. Each unit is a self-contained combat platform housing its own power supply, onboard tactical AI, sensor suite, and dual weapon systems. Squads of Vaelindor Cognyr droids operate under marine officer command, executing orders with speed and precision no organic unit can match while retaining sufficient onboard intelligence to adapt to changing battlefield conditions without requiring continuous instruction. They are expendable in a way no clone trooper is, and are deployed accordingly — absorbing fire, breaching fortified positions, and holding ground under conditions that would destroy organic combatants.

Physical Specifications

Frame & Construction

  • Height: 8 ft 2 in — slightly taller than a standard Caelyndor Marinyr marine, providing a more imposing frontline presence and a marginally larger target to draw fire away from organic squadmates.
  • Weight: 410 lbs unloaded combat configuration.
  • Frame Material: Titanium-carbide alloy skeleton with a modular composite armor shell; internal components housed in a reinforced central chassis with impact-dispersing internal mounting systems.
  • Locomotion: Bipedal leg assembly with active balance compensation; capable of traversing all terrain types encountered in standard marine operational profiles including zero-gravity, low-gravity, and atmospheric environments.
  • Hands & Manipulation: Five-fingered articulated gauntlet hands with pressure-sensitive grip modulation; capable of operating all standard marine equipment, weapons, and interfaces without modification.
  • Tactical Skirt Panel: Composite-weave lower body panel suspended from the waist assembly; provides partial coverage of the upper leg servos and internal cabling while maintaining full freedom of movement; constructed from the same material as marine combat cloaks for visual consistency.

Armor Shell

  • Helmet: Full-coverage faceted combat helm with amber/gold visor slit providing 180-degree optical coverage; rear-mounted stabilizer fins assist gyroscopic orientation in zero-gravity; visor integrates all primary sensor feeds directly into the onboard tactical processor.
  • Chest Plate: Heavy multi-layer angular plate covering the primary power cell and central processor housing; gold accent stripe running vertically down the chest serves as a visual IFF marker distinguishing Vaelindor units from enemy combatants at close range.
  • Shoulder Plates: Broad angular pauldrons providing upper arm and neck coverage; mounting points for optional equipment modules.
  • Gauntlets: Articulated armored gloves covering wrist joints and hand servos; reinforced knuckle plates.
  • Greaves & Boots: Heavy lower leg armor with reinforced boot soles designed for zero-gravity magnetic surface grip and high-impact landings.
  • Total Armor Thickness: 68 mm composite stack across primary coverage zones.

Mechanical & Systems Specifications

Power Systems

  • Primary Power Source: High-density torsion battery core housed in the central chest chassis; provides 168 hours of continuous combat operations under standard load.
  • Secondary Power: Distributed capacitor array across the limb assemblies; provides emergency burst power for weapon discharge and movement during primary cell depletion.
  • Power Recovery: Passive thermal recovery from weapons discharge and movement feeds back into the capacitor array during low-activity periods.
  • Recharge: Full recharge from ship or base power grid in 4 hours; field recharge via compatible marine high-density battery packs in 8 hours.

Propulsion & Mobility

  • Ground Mobility: Bipedal locomotion with active gyroscopic stabilization; traverses broken terrain, zero-gravity hull surfaces, and flooded or pressurized environments without modification.
  • Sprint Speed: 26–30 mph sustained; 34 mph burst.
  • Jump Capability: Vertical leap of 8 feet; horizontal leap of 16 feet under standard gravity.
  • Zero-Gravity Operation: Magnetic sole plates for hull and station surface traversal; integrated RCS micro-thrusters at hip and shoulder mounts for short-duration void maneuvering.
  • Load Capacity: Sustained carry of 705 lbs across all terrain types without performance degradation.

Sensors & Processing Systems

  • Tactical Processor: Onboard semi-autonomous AI with full ICAS-F network integration; processes threat data, terrain mapping, and squad coordination simultaneously; command override accepted from any authenticated marine officer or ICAS network node at any time.
  • Visual Suite: Full-spectrum optical sensors behind the visor slit — visible light, near-infrared, short-wave infrared, long-wave infrared, and ultraviolet; HDR processing for high-contrast environments including muzzle flash and directed-energy discharge.
  • Acoustic Suite: Directional microphone array for threat localization and communication pickup; filters background noise to isolate relevant acoustic signatures.
  • Tactical Awareness: Real-time squad mesh integration; shares sensor data with all networked units including marine ICAS overlays, Sentinel drone uplinks, and vehicle tactical systems.
  • IFF System: Active friend/foe identification broadcast and reception; cross-compatible with marine ICAS-F IFF protocols.
  • Navigation: Inertial navigation with terrain-relative optical mapping; dead-reckoning capable in full EW denial environments.

Behavioral Architecture

  • Operating Mode — Standard: Onboard AI executes assigned orders and adapts tactically within mission parameters; selects firing positions, manages cover, coordinates movement with adjacent units, and prioritizes targets according to threat assessment.
  • Operating Mode — Autonomous: Activated when communications are severed; unit continues executing last known mission objective using onboard judgment until contact is re-established or the objective is achieved.
  • Operating Mode — Slaved: Full remote operation by a designated ICAS operator; onboard AI is suspended and all movement and weapon discharge is directed externally.
  • Command Override: Any authenticated marine officer can issue direct verbal or ICAS-transmitted orders that immediately supersede onboard AI decisions; override is instantaneous with no delay or resistance from the unit.
  • Squad Coordination: Units within a squad share a continuous low-latency tactical mesh; coordinated fire, movement, and breaching actions are synchronized automatically without requiring individual orders for each unit.

Operational Directives & Behavioral Safeguards

Command Hierarchy Compliance

  • Absolute command recognition: Vaelindor Cognyr units recognize and comply with the full Caelyndor Marinyr officer hierarchy without exception; orders from authenticated officers are executed immediately and without resistance.
  • ICAS behavioral regulation: The ICAS network integration continuously monitors unit behavioral outputs and applies corrective overrides if a unit deviates from assigned mission parameters, engages unauthorized targets, or exhibits sensor malfunction-driven erratic behavior.
  • Escalation of force protocols: Units apply minimum necessary force as directed; lethal engagement requires either direct officer authorization or confirmation of hostile action against AEN personnel.

Operational Boundaries

  • Autonomy limits: Independent judgment is restricted to tactical execution — target selection within an authorized engagement zone, cover utilization, and movement pathing. Strategic decisions, rules of engagement changes, and target category expansions require officer authorization.
  • Friendly fire prevention: IFF cross-referencing is active at all times; weapon discharge against a confirmed friendly IFF signal is physically locked out at the firing system level regardless of onboard AI state.
  • Self-preservation weighting: Units do not prioritize self-preservation over mission completion or the protection of organic squadmates; a Vaelindor Cognyr will hold a position, absorb fire, or breach a fortified point at the cost of its own destruction if ordered or if doing so protects marine personnel.

Fail-Safe Protocols

  • Communication loss: Unit defaults to last confirmed order set and continues execution until contact is restored or the objective is complete.
  • Critical damage: Upon loss of primary processor function, all weapon systems are locked and the unit ceases movement to prevent uncontrolled discharge.
  • Capture prevention: If a unit detects imminent capture by hostile forces and cannot resist or withdraw, an internal destruction sequence is initiated to deny the enemy access to hardware and tactical data.
  • Remote wipe: ICAS commanders can issue a full memory and AI wipe remotely to any unit at any time.

Performance Metrics

Speed & Mobility

  • Sprint speed: 26–30 mph sustained; 34 mph burst (baseline human elite sprinter ~23 mph).
  • Acceleration: 0–25 mph in approximately 1.8 seconds.
  • Jump height: 8 feet vertical under standard gravity.
  • Agility index: Comparable to a Caelyndor Marinyr marine in open terrain; slightly less agile in confined spaces due to increased frame size.
  • Zero-gravity mobility: Full operational capability via magnetic sole plates and RCS micro-thrusters.

Strength & Power

  • Lift capacity: 705 lbs sustained carry; up to 1,760 lbs short-duration lift under burst power.
  • Strike force: Reinforced gauntlet strike delivers approximately 4× the impact force of a peak-condition Caelyndor Marinyr marine.
  • Grip strength: Sufficient to deform standard-gauge steel plating; pressure-modulated to handle sensitive equipment without damage.

Endurance & Resilience

  • Operational endurance: 168 hours continuous combat operations on primary power cell.
  • Damage tolerance: Frame remains operational after penetrating hits to non-critical limb sections; combat effectiveness is maintained until primary chassis or processor housing is compromised.
  • Thermal tolerance: Full operational performance from −112°F to 392°F.
  • Pressure tolerance: Sealed for vacuum operations; rated to 120 atmospheres external pressure for deep insertion scenarios.
  • Radiation tolerance: Hardened electronics and shielded processor housing provide operational resilience in nuclear and high-radiation environments.

Reaction & Processing Performance

  • Reaction speed: 1–3 ms from threat detection to weapon discharge initiation (baseline human ~150–250 ms).
  • Target acquisition: Full target lock within 0.4 seconds of visual contact in standard conditions.
  • Decision latency: Tactical decisions processed in under 10 ms under standard AI load.
  • Multi-target tracking: Simultaneously tracks and prioritizes up to 48 distinct targets within sensor range.

Equipment Profile

Armor System

  • VAELINDOR COMPOSITE FRAME (VCF) — Primary structural and armor shell
  • SYLRAETH-QAMAR (DQM + MAP) — Personal Shielding, compatible with marine shield system

Primary Weapon Systems

  • Standard Loadout:
    • ÆSIR-3 Beam Rifle — identical to Caelyndor Marinyr standard issue; held and operated via articulated gauntlet hands
    • VAEL-ARM-1 Integrated Directed-Energy Emitter — forearm-mounted hardlight emitter; short to medium range; used for close-quarters suppression, breaching, and point-defense; draws from the unit's capacitor array for independent discharge without depleting primary rifle power

Support Modules / Utilities

  • ICAS-COGNYR-NODE — Integrated Command & Augmentation Slot (Onboard Tactical AI Node); networked to marine ICAS-AURION-NEURO mesh for full squad integration
  • Magnetic Sole Plates — zero-gravity hull traversal
  • RCS Micro-Thruster Pack — short-duration void maneuvering at hip and shoulder mounts
  • 1 × 50 meter CNT rope with Sapphire-X Hook — matches marine standard utility kit

body:
Overview

The Vaelindor Cognyr Heavy is the direct fire support and breach counterpart to the Vaelindor Cognyr light infantry droid, sharing the same core frame architecture, behavioral systems, and manufacturing origin but built around a significantly heavier armor shell, a larger power core, and a substantially expanded weapon loadout. Where the light droid is designed to move and fight alongside marines at their pace, the heavy droid is designed to absorb punishment that would destroy any other unit on the line and keep advancing. Its thicker armor plating, broader torso, and reinforced limb construction make it visibly more imposing than the light variant, and its combination of sustained heavy machine gun fire, integrated arm emitter, and shoulder-launched missiles gives a single unit the firepower profile of a small marine fire team. Heavy droids are deployed at the point of main effort — leading breaches, anchoring defensive lines under direct fire, and suppressing fortified positions so marine squads can close and clear. They are expendable in the way no clone trooper is, and are used accordingly.

Physical Specifications

Frame & Construction
