title: Varantharissë Calantharë — Dominion of the Eternal Burning
designation: Varantharindë — The Sand Elves of Varanthas
classification: General Archive
body:
I. OVERVIEW AND CLASSIFICATION 

ATTRIBUTEdescription
Common Designations Varantharindë (People of the Eternal Burning); Sand Elves; Desert Elves
Classification Terrestrial Mammal, Elven Lineage (Taralindë Descent)
Home System  Calvareth (Homeworld: Varanthas)
Capital Varanthos Dur, Calvareth System (primary clan seat; no unified capital)
Governing Body  Clan councils of elders and memory-singers; no unified inter-clan authority
Current Leader  Position of Durvanthar vacant since the death of Varathar Kael
Average Lifespan Approximately 550 years (Biologically Immortal)
Primary Languages  Varanthi (drifted Eldarindëva); dialects vary between Varanthos Dur and Varanthos Vel

The Varantharindë are the descendants of a High Elf colonial expedition that lost contact with Arandorë Eldainë during the chaos of the Aevum Belli and was presumed lost. They were not lost. Over the millennia of isolation that followed, the population adapted to the conditions of Varanthas with a thoroughness that has produced a lineage recognizably elven in its foundations but shaped by their world in ways that distinguish them clearly from any other branch of elvenkind. The Loremasters record their rediscovery as one of the most significant events of the current period, and note that the complexity of what follows from it has not yet fully presented itself.


 Their civic status within the Realm has not been formally determined, which reflects the reality of the situation more than any administrative oversight. The Varantharindë were a colony presumed lost during one of the most catastrophic periods in elven history, and the Realm that rediscovered them is not the same Realm that lost contact with them. Thousands of years separate those two moments and everything about both parties has changed in the intervening time. The relationship is being built carefully and without assumptions, and the Loremasters consider it important that this record reflect that complexity honestly rather than paper over it with institutional language that the circumstances do not support.


The name Varantharindë, meaning People of the Eternal Burning, is the designation they use for themselves. It was not given to them and it does not reference their origins in Arandorë Eldainë. It references Varanthas, which is the more important point. These are a people who named themselves after the world that shaped them rather than the civilization that produced them, and that choice says more about who they became during their millennia of isolation than any biological classification or lineage record can. The Loremasters use the name throughout this record accordingly, and note that the Varantharindë would find any other designation both inaccurate and unwelcome.

II. PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION AND BIOLOGY 

characteristicdescription
Height, Male 5'10" to 6'4" (177 to 193 cm)
Height, Female 5'8" to 6'2" (172 to 188 cm)
Weight, Male 120 to 165 lb (54.4 to 74.8 kg)
Weight, Female 110 to 150 lb (49.9 to 68 kg)
Skin Deep amber, ochre, and burnt sienna; faint residual luminescence in oldest individuals only
Hair Black, deep brown, and dark auburn most common; bleached lighter with prolonged surface exposure
Eyes Pale silver, near-white, and light grey; adapted for high-intensity light; luminescence largely absent
Diet Omnivorous; arthropod-based staple diet; heightened toxin resistance; adapted to extreme nutritional scarcity

The Varantharindë carry the biological architecture of the Taralindë in their foundations and Varanthas in everything built on top of it. They are shorter than the High Elves by a meaningful margin, leaner in frame, and built through the muscle in a way that reflects generations of survival in one of the harshest environments in the known galaxy rather than the architectural grandeur of Anorvalas. The divergence is not subtle enough to require close inspection. Side by side with a Taralindë, a Varantharindë reads as clearly the same species and clearly not the same people. 


Their skin runs in the warm deep tones of desert rock and dried earth, the result of millennia of adaptation to Calanthar's relentless intensity and the reflected heat of canyon stone. The luminescence that defines the Taralindë's physical presence has in most Varantharindë reduced to a biological trace, present in the oldest individuals in moments of strong emotion or deep darkness but otherwise gone. The High Elves glow because Farnunsa shaped them from the living world and the light stayed in them. The Varantharindë's light dimmed over thousands of years of isolation on a world that asks everything of the people who live on it. Whether that means something theologically is a question the record does not answer. 


Their eyes adapted early in the isolation period to the problem of surviving under two suns. The vivid sapphires and emeralds of the Taralindë gave way to pale silver and near-white, with pupils that contract to near-pinpoints under direct light and open wide in darkness, managing the extraordinary light intensity of Varanthas during the day and the absolute dark of true night with equal efficiency. It is one of the more visible markers of how completely the planet shaped them, and one of the first things High Elf observers noted on initial contact.


Like all elven lineages, the Varantharindë are biologically immortal. Their cells do not degrade with age and there is no equivalent of senescence in their biology. The average lifespan figure reflects Varanthas rather than biology: the planet kills people at a consistent rate through heat, dehydration, the planet's apex fauna, and the particular hazards of a civilization built inside canyon rock below one of the most hostile terrain environments in the known galaxy. The oldest Varantharindë alive today carry within them an unbroken memory of events going back to before the Realm lost contact with the colony. The Loremasters regard those individuals as primary sources of considerable significance and are currently in the early stages of attempting to access those memories through whatever channel the relevant clan leaders will permit.

III. CULTURE AND VALUES 

Everything the Varantharindë value traces back to the same source, Varanthas does not forgive inattention, and the people who have lived on it long enough have organized their entire existence around that fact. Knowledge is not abstract to them the way it is institutional to the High Elves. It is immediate and practical and the difference between having it and not having it is often the difference between coming back from the basin and not coming back. The memory-singers are not archivists in the Taralindë sense. They are living repositories of survival information, and the culture that produced them treats the accumulation and transmission of what is known with the same urgency that other civilizations treat the stockpiling of weapons or food.


The memory-singer role is the closest thing the Varantharindë have to a universal institution across clan lines. Every clan has them. Every clan protects them above almost anyone else in the community because what they carry cannot be reconstructed if it is lost. Aquifer locations, basin crossing routes, the behavioral patterns of named Kaldrath, the territorial ranges of known Varath, the history of every significant event the clan has experienced going back as far as the oldest living member's memory extends and then as far back as the oral record before that: all of it lives in the memory-singers, maintained through regular recitation and cross-checked between individuals to catch drift before it becomes distortion. It is a system built by people who watched what happens when records burn and decided that the only truly safe archive is one that breathes.


Their relationship with the planet's apex fauna defines their culture in ways that no other single factor does. The Varath are the Great Changers, divine in the Varantharindë understanding, not worshipped with ceremony but revered with a quality of attention that amounts to the same thing. The Kaldrath shares the canyon with them and is treated as a neighbor whose habits are worth understanding and whose presence is worth acknowledging. The Caerveth nests above their cities and is hunted with the same hands that regard the hunting as something that needs to be done carefully and with awareness of what it costs. The Varantharindë do not separate the sacred from the practical. On Varanthas they are the same thing.


The crossing guides occupy a specific cultural position that has no direct equivalent in any other elven lineage. They are the people who transit the basin, who work with Varath, who maintain the waypoint outposts and build the crossing records that the memory-singers fold into the broader knowledge base. Their status is earned through demonstrated survival over years of the most demanding work the culture produces, and it is not transferable through lineage or appointment. A clan leader's child who cannot cross the basin is not a crossing guide. This is understood and unremarkable. The Varantharindë have been on Varanthas long enough to know what happens when you put people in roles they have not earned.


The division between clans is real and in some cases runs deep. The clans of Varanthos Dur and Varanthos Vel have developed differently enough over the millennia that the cultural gap between them is wider than the physical basin that separates their continents. Dur clans tend toward older and more elaborate governance structures, deeper canyon cities, and a conservatism about change that reflects the age and stability of the rock they live in. Vel clans are faster to adapt, more willing to abandon what is not working, and more practiced at the kind of rapid improvisation that their younger and less stable geology requires. Neither characterization is a criticism in Varantharindë terms. Both are observations about what different environments produce in people over enough time.

IV. HISTORY AND ORIGINS 

The origins of the Varantharindë lie in a High Elf colonial expedition dispatched during the Aevum Concordiäte to survey and establish a presence in the Calvareth system. The expedition made contact with Varanthas, found it habitable in the technical sense that it could support elven life, and established the first settlements in the canyon systems of what would become Varanthos Dur. Contact with Arandorë Eldainë was maintained for a period whose length the surviving Varantharindë oral record is imprecise about, and then the Aevum Belli arrived and the contact stopped. The Realm assumed the colony had not survived. The colony did not know what the Realm assumed because the colony had stopped receiving transmissions and had more immediate problems to address. 


The early period of isolation on Varanthas was the hardest. The colony had arrived with technology and resources suited to a civilization with supply lines and institutional support, and found itself suddenly without either on a planet that requires its inhabitants to know exactly what they are doing at all times. The oral record of this period, preserved in the memory-singers of the oldest Dur clans, describes losses that reduced the original population to a fraction of what had landed. What survived was the fraction that learned fastest, and what they learned fastest was that Varanthas rewards specific and practical knowledge above everything else and has no interest in the kind of general competence that works well enough everywhere else. 


The transition from colony to indigenous civilization is not a clean line in the Varantharindë's own understanding of their history. There was no moment when they decided to stop being High Elves stranded on a difficult world and start being the Varantharindë. It happened gradually, through the accumulation of generations of people who had never known anything else, who learned Varanthas the way children learn their native language rather than the way adults learn a second one. By the time anyone alive could remember the original colony, the memory existed only in the memory-singers' oral record rather than in living experience, and the question of what they had been before they were what they were had become more historical than personal.


Varathar Kael, the Durvanthar, is the central figure of Varantharindë history and the only person the oral record treats as having genuinely changed the trajectory of the civilization. He came from among the crossing guides, which is the detail the memory-singers always lead with when they recount his story, because it matters to them that the man who unified the clans came from the most earned and least hereditary role their culture produces. He spent his early life crossing the basin and building the kind of reputation that travels across clan lines, which on Varanthas means surviving long enough and doing it well enough that people who have never met you know your name. The crisis that drove him to ride the grandfather Varath came from outside the planet, an external threat whose nature the memory-singers preserve in full but which this record summarizes as a force the clans could not meet individually and survive. What Varathar Kael did in response to it is the defining event of Varantharindë history. What happened after his death, the return of divided political and spiritual authority to their separate and often competing positions, is the defining condition of Varantharindë governance ever since.


The rediscovery came without warning from the Varantharindë's perspective, which is an experience they have processed differently depending on the clan and the individual. The Realm arrived with the full weight of its institutional presence and the news that the people of Varanthas were descended from a colony that had been lost and forgotten, which is information that lands differently for different people. Some of the clan leaders have received Realm representatives with the cautious openness of people who recognize that the wider galaxy exists and that engaging with it on reasonable terms is better than the alternative. Others have declined contact entirely and have made their position on the subject clear in terms that the Office of Foreign Affairs has relayed to the Loremasters without editorial. The Loremasters record both responses without preference. The Varantharindë spent thousands of years building something on Varanthas without any help from the Realm that left them there, and their feelings about the reunion are their own business to work through at whatever pace they choose.

title: Calathirion-class Energy Lance
classification: Tri-Mode Free-Electron Laser Turret System
role: Primary directed-energy weapon system for all AEN naval combatants from corvette to dreadnought class. Tri-mode free-electron laser operating at 13.5 nm (EUV) for vacuum engagement, 1,064 nm (near-IR) for standard atmospheric engagement, and 1,550 nm (short-IR) for humid and maritime atmospheric engagement. Dual-mirror carousel turret design enables mode switching without crew intervention. Scaled across six marks to match hull class power generation and turret volume constraints
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Vaelnarion-class Particle Lance
classification: Neutral Hydrogen Relativistic Particle Beam — Turret-Mounted System
role: Primary crew-neutralization and electronics-kill weapon system for all AEN naval combatants from corvette to supercarrier class. Keel-mounted dielectric laser accelerator feeding beam-transport turrets via 30 T REBCO high-temperature superconducting dipole magnet arcs. Fires neutralized hydrogen atoms at relativistic velocities. Kill mechanism operates through muon radiation produced by hadronic pion cascades in the target hull, delivering lethal ionizing radiation through any thickness of armor. Designed for vacuum-only operation. Designed for combined employment with the Calathirion-class Tri-Mode Lance to present defenders with an unsolvable dual-threat engagement.
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Aethrandor-class Revolver Launch System
classification: Electromagnetic Rotary Magazine Launch System — Ship-Mounted
role: Primary munition delivery system for all ship-launched ordnance in the AEN fleet. Each unit consists of a coilgun launch barrel backed by a rotary magazine drum that indexes munitions into the breech sequentially. The coilgun barrel provides first-stage electromagnetic acceleration to 3–15 km/s depending on munition mass, eliminating the need for booster stages and providing high initial velocity at zero propellant cost to the munition. The rotary drum feeds the next round into the breech immediately after firing, enabling sustained launch rates with near-zero downtime between shots. Compatible with all AEN ship-launched ordnance: Umbraelin torpedoes, Aelvorin missiles, Morvaelin Casaba lances, and Naelvorin kinetic penetrators. Multiple Revolver units are installed per ship, scaled to hull class.
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Umbraelin-class Torpedo
classification: Stealth Nuclear Torpedo — Ship-Launched System
role: Stealth nuclear strike weapon for all AEN naval combatants from destroyer to dreadnought class. Radar-absorbing composite hull with near-zero thermal signature during unpowered ballistic coast phase. Launched hours before engagement on pre-calculated intercept trajectories via Aethrandor-class Revolver Launch System. Passive infrared terminal homing activates at 50–100 km, transitioning to active LIDAR in final 5 km. Terminal solid motor burn provides closing velocity in final seconds, minimizing point defense reaction time. Contact or proximity detonation delivers full nuclear yield at zero standoff. Designed to arrive undetected while enemy attention is focused on energy weapon engagement and missile
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Aelvorin-class Missile
classification: Nuclear Saturation Assault Missile — Ship and Strike Craft Launched
role: Saturation nuclear strike weapon for all AEN naval combatants and strike craft. Fired in coordinated salvos of 8–24+ rounds via Aethrandor-class Revolver Launch System, timed to arrive simultaneously from multiple launch vectors. Coilgun launch with immediate solid motor burn provides maximum closing velocity and minimum flight time, giving enemy point defense minimal reaction window. Mixed warhead yields within each salvo prevent the defender from prioritizing intercepts. Yields scaled to guarantee destructive effect against meters-thick composite armor through contact detonation, with sufficient margin for structural damage at forced standoff detonation. Designed to overwhelm point defense through volume and force the defender to engage every inbound track without knowing which carries the heaviest warhead.
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Morvaelin-class Casaba Lance
classification: Nuclear Shaped Charge Directed Plasma Lance — Ship and Strike Craft Launched
role: Directed nuclear armor-piercing weapon for all AEN naval combatants and strike craft. A nuclear device detonates behind a precision-machined concave tungsten liner, converting omnidirectional nuclear yield into a focused jet of superheated tungsten plasma traveling at hundreds to thousands of kilometers per second. The jet is directed at the target hull from 5–50 km standoff, outside effective point defense engagement range. Energy density within the jet cone exceeds any known armor material's ability to survive by orders of magnitude. Scaled warheads ensure total destruction of meters-thick composite armor even at maximum standoff. Delivered via missile body for saturation approach or torpedo body for stealth approach via Aethrandor-class Revolver Launch System.
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Thalirion-class Point Defense Array
classification: Rapid-Pulse Point Defense Laser Array — Ship-Mounted
role: Primary close-in defense weapon system for all AEN naval vessels. Rapid-cycling free-electron laser turrets optimized for high slew rate, fast target acquisition, and rapid engagement of multiple simultaneous inbound threats. All detection, classification, prioritization, tracking, and engagement functions are managed by the ship's Aurion-class Intelligent Command Assistant System (ICAS). The ICAS operates the entire point defense network as a unified defensive system, coordinating all turrets simultaneously with millisecond-scale target switching and engagement sequencing that exceeds any biological operator's capability. Crew involvement is limited to setting weapons-free or weapons-hold status and designating target exclusion zones. Wavelength optimized for maximum energy coupling into missile airframes and warhead casings at engagement ranges of 50 m to 5,000 km. Designed to defeat saturation missile salvos, stealth torpedoes, Casaba lances, and kinetic penetrators across overlapping defensive zones providing full-sphere coverage around the ship.
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Falcarin-class Flak Battery
classification: Electromagnetic Rapid-Fire Fragmentation Battery — Ship-Mounted
role: Secondary close-in defense weapon system for all AEN naval vessels. Rapid-fire coilgun turrets firing proximity-fused fragmentation rounds that detonate in the path of incoming threats, creating a debris cloud of high-velocity tungsten fragments. All detection, tracking, and engagement functions are managed by the ship's Aurion-class Intelligent Command Assistant System (ICAS), which coordinates flak battery fire simultaneously with Thalirion laser point defense engagements as a unified defensive network. The ICAS calculates optimal fragment cloud placement using predictive trajectory analysis, seeding interception volumes ahead of incoming threats rather than attempting direct-hit solutions. Crew involvement is limited to setting weapons-free or weapons-hold status. Designed to complement the Thalirion laser point defense by providing a physical kill mechanism effective against threats that survive or evade laser engagement, particularly kinetic penetrators and massed salvos where fragmentation clouds cover wider intercept volumes than focused laser beams.
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Vaeryndor-class Torpedo Tube
classification: Electromagnetic Single-Shot Torpedo Launch System — Ship-Mounted
role: Dedicated heavy torpedo launch system for AEN capital ships. Single-shot superconducting coilgun tubes designed specifically for Umbraelin-class T-2 and T-3 torpedoes that exceed the Aethrandor-class Revolver Launch System's mass capacity. Each tube is loaded individually from the ship's magazine by automated handling equipment managed by the Aurion-class ICAS. Provides electromagnetic first-stage acceleration at zero propellant cost to the torpedo. Tubes are sealed behind armored doors that open only during launch to minimize hull vulnerability. Designed for deliberate, pre-planned torpedo deployment rather than rapid-fire salvo operations — the weapon's stealth coast doctrine means torpedoes are launched hours before engagement on pre-calculated intercept trajectories, making rapid reload unnecessary.
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Aurelion Photonic-Boson Lattice (APBL)
classification: Structural Photonic Condensate System — Ship and Installation Integrated
role: Modular photonic condensate lattice for structural reinforcement, hull restoration, architectural construction, and defensive barrier generation. Each emitter node generates a tessellated tile of coherent photonic structure that exerts mechanical force on matter, producing a rigid, load-bearing surface. The lattice can be reconfigured in milliseconds, providing rapid-response structural capability for damage control, field construction, emergency hull integrity restoration, and permanent architectural integration. Used across AEN naval vessels, orbital stations, and planetary infrastructure as both a complement to physical construction materials and a standalone structural system.
opStatus: Active Service — Fleet Engineering and Infrastructure Standard

title: Sulindor-class Magnetic Sail Drive
classification: Magnetospheric Plasma Propulsion and Q-Drive System — Ship-Mounted
role: Primary interplanetary and interstellar cruise propulsion system for all AEN naval vessels from corvette to supercarrier class. Dual-regime system operating in passive magnetic sail mode (fuel-free momentum capture from stellar wind) and active Q-Drive mode (energy extraction from streaming medium to accelerate onboard propellant, enabling velocities exceeding the medium's own speed). The ship's Vaelnarion-class dielectric laser accelerator serves as the Q-Drive's propellant ejector, providing continuously variable exhaust velocity matched to ship speed. Hydrogen Ram Intake (HRI) collects ambient hydrogen for reactor fuel and Q-Drive propellant replenishment during transit.
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Galthorion-class Combat Magnetosphere
classification: Superconducting Hull-Integrated Magnetic Defense Field — Ship-Mounted
role: Dedicated charged particle defense system for all AEN naval vessels. REBCO high-temperature superconducting coils integrated into the hull structure generate a sustained magnetic field envelope surrounding the ship. Incoming charged particles are deflected along curved trajectories that carry them past the ship without contacting the hull. Field strength and depth optimized for combat-relevant particle energies up to ~5 TeV. Separate system from the Sulindor-class Magnetic Sail Drive, which retracts during combat. The combat magnetosphere activates during combat and remains compatible with all AEN weapons systems. Forces any adversary to neutralize their particle beams before firing or accept complete deflection.
opStatus: Active Service — AEN Strategic Battlegroup Standard

title: Aurëndril-class Composite Armor System
classification: Multi-Layer Composite Hull Armor — Ship-Integrated
role: Primary passive defense system for all AEN naval vessels. Five-layer composite armor with integrated Whipple gap, engineered to defeat kinetic penetrators through ceramic disruption and hydrodynamic depth, resist directed energy weapons through ablation and thermal management, absorb nuclear weapon neutron radiation through distributed boron-10 capture, and attenuate secondary gamma radiation through gadolinium capture layer.
